title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: S&P 500 (+1.0%), Nasdaq (+1.4%) and Dow (+624 pts/+1.2%) rallied for a second straight session Thursday after Fed Governor Waller said he'd support holding rates steady this month if August inflation data cooperates, easing rate-hike fears tied to the oil-driven inflation scare.
Markets: The 10-year Treasury yield eased to 4.76% after touching its highest level since last year earlier in the week; gold jumped 2.4% to ~$4,519/oz and crude held near $91.70/bbl.
Markets: All eyes are on today's August jobs report (8:30am ET) — the last major data point before the Fed's Sept 16 rate decision.
Companies: Nvidia agreed to buy Hugging Face for about $12.9 billion, its largest deal since the 2020 Mellanox acquisition, deepening its foothold in open-weight AI models; Nvidia shares rose 1.8%.
Companies: Uber is cutting about 10% of its workforce as part of a broader corporate shift away from 'micro-team' management structures with just one or two direct reports.

Macro/Policy: Bets on a September Fed rate hike have pared back after Waller's dovish-leaning comments, though the Sept 16 decision still hinges on today's jobs data and how oil-driven inflation pressures evolve.
